analysis:
Michael Johnson, a 9-year-old 3rd-grade student, demonstrates a strong aptitude for social skills but struggles with math word problems due to reading comprehension issues at a 1st-grade level. Despite this challenge, he performs at a mid-2nd grade level in math calculation and can solve 2-digit addition with regrouping with 80% accuracy. In terms of reading fluency, Michael reads at a rate of 45 words per minute.

To address his needs, Michael's goals include improving his reading fluency to 80 words per minute and increasing his accuracy in solving one-step word problems to 70%. These goals align well with his current performance levels and will help bridge the gap between his math calculation skills and reading comprehension abilities.

In order to support Michael in reaching his goals, he receives accommodations such as having math tests read aloud to him, extended time for testing (1.5x), and small group testing. Additionally, he receives speech therapy for 30 minutes per week to further enhance his communication skills.

Overall, Michael's strengths lie in his social skills, and with the appropriate supports and interventions in place, such as accommodations and services, he is well-positioned to make significant progress in his reading fluency and math problem-solving abilities. By leveraging his strengths and addressing his needs, Michael can work towards achieving his academic goals and continue to grow and succeed in his educational journey.
